claims.text: HfNbTiVAl10 was experimentally synthesized with a hierarchical heterostructure.
Elastic constants, misfit volumes, surface energies, and unstable stacking-fault energies can be obtained using first-principles calculations.
Physical models combining linear elasticity and microscopic principles can use DFT-accessible material parameters to describe alloy strengthening and ductility.
Misfit volumes are relevant inputs to strengthening models, while surface and unstable stacking-fault energies are relevant inputs to ductility models.
A DFT-calibrated, microstructure-informed continuum framework can predict Young's modulus, yield strength, and fracture-related behavior of HfNbTiVAl10.
Models specifically adjusted using microstructural descriptors can represent the hierarchical heterostructure of HfNbTiVAl10.
The hierarchical heterostructure contains nanoscale precipitates and phase interfaces.
Nanoscale precipitates and phase interfaces mediate localized stress distributions and dislocation behavior in HfNbTiVAl10.
The localized stress distributions and dislocation behavior are essential to the alloy's tensile and fracture performance.
The simplified models capture the key solid-solution, strengthening, and fracture mechanisms without full-scale atomistic simulation.
Explicit evaluation of alloy fracture or yield strength is mostly beyond available DFT implementations.
The integrated model will outperform established full-scale simulations in predictive accuracy across tensile and fracture properties.
The integrated model will predict Young's modulus, yield strength, and fracture metrics within ±10% of experimental measurements.
The integrated model will reduce simulation runtime by roughly an order of magnitude relative to conventional DFT or detailed finite-element simulations.
Conventional full-scale DFT, atomistic, or detailed finite-element simulations require significantly longer runtimes.
Unmodeled multiscale defects or phase transitions can cause the framework to fail when they deviate from its calibration set.
Large microstructural variation can prevent the simplified models from predicting the alloy accurately.
The ±10% accuracy target and order-of-magnitude runtime target are based on preliminary analogies with similar high-entropy-alloy systems.
Independent tensile and fracture measurements on similarly prepared HfNbTiVAl10 samples can test the model's property predictions.
The hypothesis is predeclared as falsified if any predicted mechanical property differs by more than ±10% from measurement or if runtime reduction is less than tenfold.
